title: IELTS Listening: Map and Plan Labelling
summary: How to nail map, plan and diagram labelling questions by orienting first and following the speaker's directions in order.

nodes.label: Orient first
nodes.note: Find the start point, entrance or compass before audio

nodes.label: Direction words
nodes.note: left, opposite, beyond, next to, at the end of

nodes.label: Follow in order
nodes.note: Labels come in the order the speaker moves

nodes.note: Match to given letters/words; watch spelling

chunks.heading: Orient yourself before the audio starts
chunks.body: You get a few seconds to look at the map before it's described. **Find your bearings first**: the entrance or 'you are here' point, the compass, and any labels already filled in. Knowing where you start makes the directions easy to follow.
chunks.realExample: A campsite map with the 'reception' marked and a compass in the corner? Put your finger on reception — every instruction ('past the shop, then north') now has a starting point.
chunks.memoryHook: Find 'you are here' before the voice starts. No start point, no chance.

chunks.heading: Listen for directional language
chunks.body: Map answers live in **preposition and direction words**: *opposite, next to, beyond, along, at the end of, on your left, to the north*. Pre-teach these to your ear so they don't slip past.
chunks.realExample: 'Walk along the path and the library is the second building on your right, just opposite the café.' The answer is fixed by 'second… on your right… opposite the café' — three location clues in one sentence.
chunks.memoryHook: The answer is in the prepositions. Hunt left / opposite / beyond / next to.

chunks.heading: Answers come in order — don't jump back
chunks.body: The speaker moves through the map in a **logical route**, so the labels are given in **order**. If you miss one, **leave it and move on** to the next — going back means you miss the following answer too.
chunks.realExample: Missed building C while writing B? Don't freeze — jump to D immediately. One lost label is survivable; freezing loses you three.
chunks.memoryHook: The tour only goes forward. Miss one? Let it go and catch the next.

chunks.heading: Match the given options and check spelling
chunks.body: Labelling questions usually give you a **list of options (A, B, C…)** or words to place. Write the **exact letter or word** given. Because you copy answers to the sheet at the end, **spelling counts** — a misspelt label is marked wrong.
chunks.realExample: If the option list says 'reception', don't write 'rehception' or 'front desk' — copy the given word exactly. On the paper test you also get time to transfer answers, so use it to double-check spelling.
chunks.memoryHook: Copy the option exactly. A right answer spelt wrong scores zero.

recall.q: What should you do in the seconds before a map is described?
recall.a: Orient yourself — find the starting point or entrance, the compass, and any labels already given.

recall.q: Which type of vocabulary carries most map-labelling answers?
recall.a: Directional and prepositional language: opposite, next to, beyond, along, at the end of, left/right, north/south.

recall.q: In what order do map-labelling answers appear?
recall.a: In the order the speaker moves through the map, so the answers run in sequence — don't jump back if you miss one.

recall.q: What should you do if you miss one label?
recall.a: Leave it and move straight to the next; going back usually means missing the following answer too.

recall.q: Why does spelling matter on labelling answers?
recall.a: You copy answers onto the answer sheet, and a correctly-heard but misspelt label is marked wrong.
